title: Trump Weighs Renewed Iran Strikes as Republicans Split Over War and Hegseth
dek: After Republicans lost ground in the midterms, Trump says he will decide whether to resume the Iran war or pursue a deal, while a Republican push to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gains traction.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Electronic market-price display with rows of financial information

keyPoints: The Los Angeles Times reported that the U.S. carried out limited strikes on Iran on Friday, and that officials said renewed all-out attacks remain a distinct possibility.
Trump told reporters on Thursday: “Now we will make a decision” and “You’ll know soon enough.”
Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, plans to present articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth next week, the LA Times reported.
The National reported that no order to resume military operations had been issued as of its reporting.
body:
President Donald Trump is weighing whether to resume the war with Iran or pursue an agreement, and the political ground under that choice shifted after Republicans lost ground in the midterm elections.

## Limited strikes, larger option open

The Los Angeles Times reported that the U.S. carried out limited strikes on Iran on Friday. Two U.S. officials told the paper that a renewal of all-out attacks remained a distinct possibility, and that U.S. diplomats had urged Arab counterparts to prepare for an intense period of fighting. Nonessential foreign service and intelligence personnel across the Middle East were ordered home, the paper reported.

## Trump: “You’ll know soon enough”

Speaking in the Oval Office on Thursday, Trump said: “Now we will make a decision. Do we want to go further? I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I will have to. You’ll know soon enough.” The National reported that Trump met national security advisers on Wednesday and Thursday, and that U.S. Central Command was finalizing preparations for a potential operation. Officials were still considering next steps, Fox News reported, according to The National.

## Hegseth under pressure

The LA Times reported that Massie plans to present articles of impeachment against Hegseth next week over his role overseeing the war effort, and that the measure is expected to gain enough Republican support to pass. The paper also reported that Trump has been surveying advisers about Hegseth’s performance, while publicly maintaining support for him. Hegseth has faced scrutiny over allegations that he misled Trump about the war’s risks to commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

## Vance’s position

The LA Times described a “statement of brazen defiance” from Vice President JD Vance opposing the war. In a post on X, Vance said Republican voters cast ballots for Democrats partly because of frustration over the conflict, the cost of living and U.S. support of Israel, The National reported.

## What we do not know

Meridian has not verified whether an operation is imminent, what outcome Trump will choose, or when a House impeachment vote would occur.
